group_assessment.weighting: Prospective single-centre two-period crossover pilot in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy (36 enrolled, 22 analysed; focal in 16), 16:8 time-restricted eating with or without a commercial MCT shake, seizure diary outcome. Not a WWOX system, not children, not a calorie-restriction or dextrose design. The reported fact is a non-significant difference with wide patient-level variability; the authors' words 'signal favoring IF-MCT' rest on post hoc responder counts and a Kaplan-Meier plot defined by starting sequence.

entries.proposition: The trial was a 16:8 time-restricted eating crossover in adults; no limit was placed on intake in the eating window, so it tests a timing pattern, not a calorie target.
entries.snippet: During IF, participants fasted for 16 h per day and consumed only water and unsweetened tea during the fasting window; no restrictions were imposed on food intake during the 8‐h eating window.

entries.proposition: The MCT shake added 360 kcal per 200 mL.
entries.snippet: The number of calories per 200 mL was 360 kcal.

entries.proposition: Thirty-six were enrolled and 22 analysed per protocol; three completers were excluded for adherence concerns.
entries.snippet: Of the 25 participants who completed the trial, three were excluded from the analysis owing to substantial concerns about adherence to study procedures (Figure 1).

entries.proposition: The analysed group was adult, mostly female and mostly focal epilepsy.
entries.snippet: Thus, 22 participants were included in the final analysis: 19 were female and 3 were male; 16 had focal epilepsy, 2 had generalized epilepsy, and 4 had epilepsy of undetermined type (Table 1).

entries.proposition: No difference in seizure frequency was found within participants across conditions.
entries.snippet: we found no evidence of within‐participant differences (Friedman test; p = .183)

entries.proposition: The Kaplan-Meier statement is described as an earlier effect during the combined regimen, with Breslow p = .233.
entries.snippet: In addition to the clearer seizure‐suppressive effect in the IF‐MCT condition, a Kaplan–Meier curve also indicated an earlier effect during ketogenic intermittent fasting (Breslow: p = .233).

entries.proposition: The Kaplan-Meier figure legend defines the two curves by the starting sequence (IF-MCT first versus IF first), not by condition; the curves therefore mix sequence with treatment.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3: Kaplan-Meier curves labelled Start IF-MCT and Start IF; legend text 'Blue line=IF-MCT first; red line=IF first'; the proportion not yet responding falls to about 0.55 for the IF-MCT-first sequence and about 0.73 for the IF-first sequence at week 12, with censoring marks.

experimental_context.system: adults with drug-resistant epilepsy, crossover, by starting sequence
experimental_context.endpoint: time to at least 50% seizure reduction

entries.qualifies_needle: indicated an earlier effect during ketogenic intermittent fasting

entries.proposition: Table 2 gives participant 3 as seizure-free (0, 0, 0) in all three IF-alone intervals as well as at 12 weeks of IF-MCT; the Discussion says seizure freedom occurred only during IF-MCT.
The Discussion states seizure freedom was observed only during the combined regimen.
entries.snippet: Overall, this crossover pilot trial suggests a signal favoring IF–MCT, with earlier and more frequent responder outcomes and seizure freedom observed only during IF–MCT.

entries.proposition: Participant 28 rose from 94 seizures at baseline to 216 in the first IF-MCT block and stayed above baseline in IF; two participants account for the largest counts.
The authors say the degree of ketosis might have been insufficient (peak 0.13 versus 0.06 mmol).
entries.snippet: Although IF–MCT increased BHB concentrations compared with IF (peak value IF‐MCT: 0.13 mmol vs peak value IF: 0.06 mmol; Figure 2), the degree of ketosis might have been insufficient.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 plots beta-hydroxybutyrate in micromol/L with a maximum near 420 and medians of roughly 75-90 (IF-MCT) and 30-40 (IF); the ketosis range quoted by the authors for a ketogenic state is 0.5-3.0 mmol/L.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 2: beta-hydroxybutyrate (micromol/l) boxplots, IF MCT median about 75 at 4 weeks and about 90 at 12 weeks, whisker maximum about 415; IF median about 40 and 30; axis 0 to 500.

experimental_context.system: adults with drug-resistant epilepsy, serum, after the fasting window

entries.proposition: Drop-out was 39% and the prespecified size was not reached.
entries.snippet: The trial did not reach the prespecified sample size of 28 participants, largely because of a drop‐out rate of 39% (14/36)

entries.proposition: Seizure counts came from patient-kept diaries.
entries.snippet: Seizure frequency was primarily assessed using patient‐reported seizure diaries, which are prone to under‐reporting and imprecision

entries.proposition: All participants had transient gastrointestinal effects during titration of the MCT shake.
entries.snippet: All participants experienced transient gastrointestinal side effects, predominantly fullness and mild nausea, during the titration phase.
